title: How to Prepare a Localization Project
h1: How to prepare a localization project
description: Prepare a localization project: choose markets, export text, write a glossary and style notes, give context, plan review and test in each language.
intro: Localization adapts your website, app, product or marketing for people in another country, not just by translating words but by adjusting dates, currencies, examples and tone. A localization specialist can do this well, but the quality depends on what you prepare: the text files, context, glossary and a plan for review and testing. This article walks through the preparation step by step.

faq.q: What is the difference between translation and localization?
faq.a: Translation changes the language. Localization also adapts formats, examples, images and tone so the content feels made for that market.

faq.q: Should I localize everything at once?
faq.a: Usually not. Start with the pages or screens that matter most to new customers, then expand once you see results.

faq.q: Why do I need a glossary?
faq.a: A glossary keeps product names and key terms consistent across pages and translators, which avoids confusion for customers.

faq.q: Who should review the localized text?
faq.a: Ideally a native speaker who knows your market, such as a customer or partner, in addition to the specialist.

faq.q: Do I need developers for localization?
faq.a: For websites and apps, often yes. Text must be exported and imported, and layouts must handle longer words or different scripts.
